fields.meta_title: Campaign Landing Page Builder for Email and Ads | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a campaign landing page for an email or an ad. Every signup keeps its UTM source and lands in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Campaign Landing Page That Tracks Every Channel
fields.hero_description: Describe the campaign and its offer. Emergent builds the campaign landing page and its form, and saves each signup with the channel that sent it in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Campaign Page Does With Each Click
fields.features_subheading: The email or the ad pays for the visit. The page decides what happens after it, and records where every visitor came from.
fields.feature_1:
One page for each campaign

Each campaign gets a page written around its offer, with no site menu to wander off through. Describe the email or ad behind it, and Emergent matches the headline to its promise.
fields.feature_2:
Channel saved with every signup

UTM tags on the link travel with the visitor to the page. The form stores each tag in a column of its own, and every signup row names the email, ad or post that sent it there.
fields.feature_3:
A closed state for ended offers

When the offer closes, the form gives way to a short note and a waitlist field. Readers who open an old email a week later see what happened instead of a form that goes nowhere.
fields.feature_4:
Headline variants on request

Ask for a second headline and Emergent builds the variant, splits visitors between them and counts signups for each. Remove the weaker one by prompt once the numbers settle.
fields.feature_5:
Contacts sent to your email tool

Signups reach Mailchimp or HubSpot through their APIs, with tags and fields set from the form. The next send in the campaign can target the readers who signed up, or skip them.
fields.feature_6:
Campaign code in your repository

Your GitHub repository holds the exported page and its database tables. Keep running it on Emergent under a custom domain, or deploy it next to the rest of your marketing site.

fields.tab_content_1:
Reminder emails skip readers who already reserved

Wrenfield Books has 400 signed copies of a new novel and one email to sell them with. The link opens a reservation page, and each reservation adds the tag Reserved to that reader in Mailchimp. Thursday's reminder goes only to the segment without the tag. So far, 312 copies are reserved.
fields.tab_content_2:
860 trial signups, each tagged with its channel

For its fall launch, Sablewood Software points one trial page at three channels: its newsletter, LinkedIn Ads and Google Ads. Every link carries UTM tags, and each signup saves its utm_source. Of 860 signups, 420 came by email, 260 from LinkedIn and 180 from Google.
fields.tab_content_3:
Hillcrest booked 3 tune-ups from 1,000 postcards

Four neighborhoods got 1,000 postcards each from Alderbrook Heating, all offering an $89 furnace tune-up. Each QR code opens the same page with its own tag, and the bookings table counts them by area. Hillcrest booked 3, under the owner's cutoff of 10 bookings, and comes off the next mailing.
fields.tab_content_4:
A free month after three friends buy day passes

Members of Basalt Climbing each get a personal referral link to the gym's day-pass page. Every pass bought through that link counts toward the member who shared it. Once three friends have bought one, the member gets an email with a free month of membership, and the row marks the reward as sent.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Campaign Landing Page
fields.howto_description: A campaign page turns the clicks a campaign paid for into signups you can trace. These steps start before the first link goes out and end with the budget for the next one.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Give each campaign its own page
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Repeat the promise of the ad
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Tag every link with UTM parameters
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask only what the follow-up needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: Sending an email or an ad to your homepage makes visitors hunt for the offer. A campaign page carries one offer and one action. Drop the main site menu, because every link off the page is a way to leave before reaching the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: The headline should restate what the visitor clicked, in nearly the same words. Google Ads judges landing page experience as one part of Quality Score, next to expected clickthrough rate and ad relevance. A mismatch costs you on search ads.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign to each link, with one campaign name such as fall-launch on all of them. Google Analytics reads these tags to credit visits to the campaign. Save them on the form too, and each signup carries its channel into your own table.
fields.howto_step_4_des: An email address and a first name are enough for a newsletter offer. A demo request might add company size. Every extra field gives a visitor one more reason to leave. Add one only when someone on your team acts on the answer.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Check the first screen on a phone
fields.howto_step_5_des: Open the page on a phone before launch. The headline and the button should both fit the first screen without scrolling. Set the email field to open the email keyboard and the phone field to open the number pad.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Campaign links get clicked for weeks after an offer closes, from forwarded emails and saved posts. Keep the page live with a note that the offer ended. When the next campaign starts, link the closed page to it, and late clicks still land somewhere useful.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Compare cost per signup by channel
fields.howto_step_7_des: Divide each channel's spend by the signups its UTM source brought in. A channel with cheap clicks and few signups costs more per signup than its click price suggests. Move the next budget toward the channel with the lowest cost per signup.

plan.angle: The top 10 treat this as the generic landing page query: example galleries (Unbounce, Instapage, HubSpot, Landingfolio, Dribbble) and definitions (Adobe, Wix, ActiveCampaign, Campaigner). None of them follows a campaign past the click. This page defines the term for the AI Overview, then shows four campaign types with what the page does with each response: an email offer that tags reservations back in Mailchimp, a launch that records every signup's channel from its UTM tags, a postcard mailer that counts bookings per neighborhood, and a referral drive that rewards the third friend. The how-to covers message match, UTM tagging, the form, the closed state and cost per signup by channel, and the FAQ answers the cost and ChatGPT questions searchers ask.
tab_stories: Wrenfield Books emails its subscribers about 400 signed copies of a new novel, and every reservation on the page tags that subscriber in Mailchimp, so Thursday's reminder email goes only to readers who have not reserved; 312 copies are taken.

Sablewood Software runs one trial page behind its fall launch on email, LinkedIn Ads and Google Ads, and each of the 860 signups keeps its utm_source and utm_campaign, so the dashboard splits them 420, 260 and 180 by channel.

Alderbrook Heating mails 1,000 postcards to each of four neighborhoods with an $89 furnace tune-up offer, each QR code carries its neighborhood, and the bookings table shows Hillcrest with 3 bookings, below the owner's cutoff of 10, so it comes off the next mailing.
Basalt Climbing gives every member a personal referral link, counts day passes bought through it, and emails a free month to the member once three friends have bought one.
